findings.affected_surface: Ruby public method on Integer class
findings.old_behavior: Integer does not have a bit_count method; calling it raises NoMethodError.
findings.new_behavior: Integer#bit_count returns the population count (number of set bits) of the integer's binary representation. Raises ArgumentError for negative integers.
findings.compatibility_reason: Purely additive API change. A new public method Integer#bit_count is introduced. No existing API, contract, or behavior is modified. Existing code that does not call bit_count is unaffected. In rare cases where a subclass or monkey-patch defined bit_count on Integer, the built-in method would override it, but this is an edge case and the change follows the standard pattern for Ruby feature additions.

findings.why_not_internal_only: The method is publicly registered via rb_define_method on rb_cInteger, making it part of the Ruby core API surface visible to all Ruby code. The C implementation functions (rb_int_bit_count, rb_big_bit_count) are in internal headers, but the Ruby method Integer#bit_count is public.
findings.uncertainty: Low uncertainty. The change is purely additive with no modification to existing interfaces. The only potential edge case is overriding of existing monkey-patches, which is inherent to Ruby language evolution.
findings.recommended_review: No manual review required. Standard additive feature addition with dedicated tests.
findings.test_recommendation: Run existing test_bit_count and test_bit_count_for_negative_numbers tests in test/ruby/test_integer.rb to verify fixnum and bignum behavior, including boundary conditions (0, positive integers, negative integer rejection). Also verify via direct smoke programs that Integer#bit_count returns correct values for common cases.
